study: OULAD real student-offering bridge repair with selective quarantine
dataset: All 32593 studentInfo enrolments; original student and module-presentation identities, all four final_result strata. No generated edges, clustering, duplicated rows or selected participants.
motivation: A deployment policy requiring both students and module-presentations to be disjoint across retained partitions. This is stronger than ordinary student-only generalization and is evaluated as a policy stress test, not an inferred leakage definition.
scenarios: For each seed randomly permute sorted 22 offering IDs, array_split into five folds, all 20 ordered test/validation fold pairs; 40 total. Original assignment by offering; every test-fold row locked. Remaining rows may be train, validation or quarantine.
objective: retained_rows_moved + 10 * newly_quarantined_rows; changed_rows includes both, reported separately
comparison: Per comparator paired-valid objective reduction and best-valid greedy portfolio. Also report validity out of all40, solver status/gap, quarantine, retained movement and changed rows. Invalid or no-incumbent cases excluded from objective ratios but retained in denominators.
interpretation: Exploratory new task; no percentage target selected or guaranteed, no replacement of prior results, no automatic repository changes. Greedy algorithms are new multi-group/quarantine extensions, not unchanged single-group adapters.
runtime: Total preprocessing plus execution recorded; solver/search budget reported separately. Concurrent jobs share a host, so wall time is descriptive only.
